purpose: Step 2 - audit lib/extraction/** vs lib/contract-model/** (both the quarantined legacy compiler generation and the new, deterministic-substrate generation this workstream wires live) and determine, from the real code and real schema (not from prose claims), who owns each kind of truth going forward.
methodology: For each candidate 'truth' kind, found every real Prisma model that could plausibly hold it, then grep-traced every real WRITER of that model (not just its readers) across lib/, app/, and scripts/, to determine which pipeline generation, if any, actually populates it TODAY from a live application path versus only from an offline script or hand-authored seed.

ownershipTable.truthKind: Document ingestion (the uploaded bytes themselves, and the Document row identifying them)
ownershipTable.owner: lib/onboarding/documents.ts + lib/connectors/upload-connector.ts (SHARED by both pipelines - genuinely one ingestion layer, not disjoint)
ownershipTable.evidence: Both lib/extraction/** and this workstream's new lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts read the SAME Document.storageRef and re-derive text via the SAME lib/extraction/parse.ts's parseDocument - this layer was already unified before this workstream began, and this workstream deliberately did not duplicate it (see 15-live-contract-analysis-orchestrator.json's documentIngestionDesign).
ownershipTable.goingForward: Unchanged, already-correct shared ownership. No decision needed here.

ownershipTable.truthKind: Structural source truth (section/article/clause boundaries, defined-term/reference DETECTION)
ownershipTable.owner: lib/contract-model/compiler/stage-structure.ts + structural-definitions.ts + structural-references.ts + structural-index.ts (the deterministic Phase 2A substrate) - NOW live-wired and persisted via this workstream's own orchestrator calling persistStructuralNodes into DocumentNode.
ownershipTable.priorState: lib/extraction/chunk.ts's own heading-detection (ARTICLE_RE/SECTION_RE/ALL_CAPS_HEADING_RE) is a SEPARATE, cruder, non-persisted chunking heuristic used only to size LLM-extraction batches - it was never a source of structural TRUTH, only a batching convenience. Phase 2A's structural index (nodeType/parentId/ordinal, DocumentNode rows) is the genuinely richer, occurrence-safe structural model, but before this workstream it was never live-populated for a real uploaded document at all (only by scripts/tests).
ownershipTable.goingForward: lib/contract-model/compiler/**'s structural substrate is now the authoritative, live structural truth for every document analyzed through the new orchestrator. lib/extraction/chunk.ts's own heading detection remains a legitimate, separate, lower-fidelity mechanism scoped ONLY to sizing the legacy extraction pipeline's own LLM batches - it makes no truth claim beyond that and this workstream leaves it untouched.

ownershipTable.truthKind: Candidate extraction (a proposed defined term / covenant rule / document relationship, awaiting human review)
ownershipTable.owner: lib/extraction/** (ExtractionCandidate, ExtractionRun/ExtractionStage) remains the SOLE live-wired human-review-and-promotion pipeline today.
ownershipTable.evidence: lib/onboarding/review.ts's reviewCandidate + lib/onboarding/promotion.ts's promoteApprovedCandidate are the only live code path that turns an AI proposal into DefinedTerm rows the legacy engine can use, gated by an explicit human APPROVE/REJECT/EDIT decision (CandidateReviewEvent audit trail) - a mature, already-correct human-in-the-loop design this workstream does not touch or duplicate.
ownershipTable.newPipelineEquivalent: lib/contract-model/compiler/discovery/** (DiscoveredCandidate) is the NEW generation's own candidate-extraction concept - richer (families/roles/normalization provenance, occurrence-safe node ids) but, critically, has NO human review/promotion UI or persisted review-decision trail of its own anywhere in this codebase (grep-confirmed: DiscoveredCandidate is never persisted to any table; it exists only in-memory for the duration of one analysis run).
ownershipTable.goingForward: lib/extraction/** remains the sole owner of the HUMAN-REVIEWABLE candidate-extraction workflow (ExtractionCandidate + CandidateReviewEvent) for the foreseeable future - this workstream does not build a competing review UI for DiscoveredCandidate (explicitly out of scope: 'no UI work'). The two candidate concepts are NOT reconciled by this workstream and remain genuinely disjoint; a future phase that wants human review of DiscoveredCandidate output would need its own new review surface, analogous to but not the same as promotion.ts's existing one.

ownershipTable.truthKind: Operative contract truth (which text is CURRENTLY governing, given amendments/supersession)
ownershipTable.owner: lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/** (OperativeContractState) - the ONLY real, occurrence-safe operative-state model in this codebase.
ownershipTable.evidence: The legacy extraction pipeline has NO operative-state concept at all - Document.effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/supersedesDocumentId (the OLD, pre-onboarding-pipeline amendment-precedence mechanism lib/covenant-engine.ts's own load layer still consults) is a coarse, WHOLE-DOCUMENT-granularity date filter with no per-provision resolution, and is populated only by hand for engineer-authored companies (Coherent/Matthews) - grep-confirmed zero live writers of effectiveFrom/effectiveTo/supersedesDocumentId in app/.
ownershipTable.goingForward: lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/** is the sole authoritative operative-state model going forward. This workstream's orchestrator computes and uses it live for every analyzed instrument (null when the instrument was never amended, a legitimate state). Document.effectiveFrom/effectiveTo remains a SEPARATE, coarser mechanism this workstream does not touch, still consulted only by the pre-existing legacy covenant-engine load path for hand-seeded companies.

ownershipTable.truthKind: Semantic claim truth (the actual compiled covenant logic - IRRule/IRDefinition - 'this section IS a $10M debt basket')
ownershipTable.owner: NONE, DURABLY, TODAY - the single most important disclosed finding of this map.
ownershipTable.evidence: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/compile.ts's own header comment discloses this by design: 'PERSISTENCE (task §34) - none in V1, by deliberate design... A SemanticCompilationCache interface... is the documented persistence-design decision: an in-memory Map implementation is provided for this phase's own resumability/idempotency proof.' Grep-confirmed: IRRule/IRDefinition objects are never written to any Prisma table anywhere in this codebase. Separately, the LEGACY quarantined compiler (lib/contract-model/compiler/orchestrator.ts) DOES persist a DIFFERENT, older shape (CandidateContractRule -> ContractRule Prisma rows, via persistContractRules in compiler/persistence.ts) - but that persistence function is called ONLY by the quarantined orchestrator (grep-confirmed sole caller), which app/** is mechanically forbidden from importing (tests/foundation-audit/legacy-phase-c-quarantine.test.ts). This workstream's new live orchestrator deliberately does NOT call persistContractRules/persistDefinedTerms/persistReferences (the legacy Phase-B persistence functions) - doing so would mean writing CandidateContractRule-shaped data derived from a candidate that was never itself produced through that legacy shape's own pipeline, silently conflating two different candidate-identity schemes into one table. The net effect: for a document analyzed ONLY through this workstream's new live path, the ContractRule/DefinedTermNode(beyond structural detection)/ContractReferenceEdge(beyond structural detection) tables remain EMPTY.
ownershipTable.whatIsPersistedInstead: Only the NEGATIVE/uncertain signal (ClaimReviewItem, for a claim needing review) and the STRUCTURAL/RELATIONSHIP facts (DocumentNode, DebtInstrument, DocumentRelationshipEdge, AmendmentEffect) are durably persisted by the live path today. A claim that reaches FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED (genuinely trusted, per 17-live-safe-failure-wiring.json's negative-case proof) produces NO durable record of its own POSITIVE content anywhere - only the absence of a ClaimReviewItem for it.
ownershipTable.goingForward: This is explicitly OUT OF THIS WORKSTREAM'S CHARTER to fix - BLOCKER-10 asks this workstream to WIRE the existing modules together, never to re-architect one of them (compile.ts's own header comment already correctly describes durable IR persistence as future work, 'a drop-in swap, not a redesign', for a LATER phase to build). This map discloses it prominently because it materially affects what 'REMEDIATED' can honestly claim: BLOCKER-10's own charter is specifically about the safe-failure/review path reaching a live trigger (which is now true and proven - 17-live-safe-failure-wiring.json), not about the compiled semantic IR itself becoming durably queryable capacity truth (which remains a separate, larger, disclosed future-phase gap, tracked here for whoever picks it up next).

ownershipTable.truthKind: Review state (an unresolved/uncertain claim awaiting a decision)
ownershipTable.owner: lib/contract-model/compiler/safe-failure/** (ClaimReviewItem/ClaimReviewObservation/ClaimReviewDecision) - now the sole live-wired review-state model for the new pipeline's own output, reached via this workstream's orchestrator.
ownershipTable.distinctFrom: lib/onboarding/review.ts's CandidateReviewEvent/ExtractionCandidate.reviewStatus - the legacy pipeline's OWN, separate, older review-state model, still live and still the correct model for ExtractionCandidate-shaped proposals. The two review-state models are NOT unified and track fundamentally different things: CandidateReviewEvent records a human's APPROVE/REJECT/EDIT decision on a proposed fact; ClaimReviewItem records the PIPELINE'S OWN detected uncertainty about a claim, independent of whether a human has looked at it yet (its own status starts at OPEN_REVIEW, not 'proposed').
ownershipTable.goingForward: Both remain correct, live, and appropriately scoped to their own pipeline generation. No reconciliation is needed or attempted by this workstream - they answer different questions ("did a human approve this AI proposal" vs. "does the pipeline itself believe this claim needs a human to look at it").

theActualDecision.question: Given the certification's own finding that these are currently totally disjoint (zero shared imports), which pipeline is THIS workstream's new orchestrator authoritative for, and why?
theActualDecision.answer: lib/contract-model/compiler/** (via this workstream's new lib/contract-model/analysis/orchestrator.ts) is now the live, authoritative production entry point for STRUCTURAL, PACKAGE-RELATIONSHIP, OPERATIVE-STATE, and REVIEW-STATE truth (the four ownership rows above where a real decision was made), confirmed correct rather than assumed - exactly per the task's own suggested direction, and confirmed honest by the fact that this decision required disclosing, not hiding, that CANDIDATE-EXTRACTION truth (lib/extraction/**) and SEMANTIC-CLAIM/CAPACITY truth (durable IRRule storage) are each owned by neither pipeline cleanly today: candidate-extraction remains lib/extraction/**'s own, separate, correctly-functioning human-review workflow (not superseded, not duplicated); durable semantic-claim persistence is owned by NEITHER pipeline today (a genuine gap, disclosed above, out of this workstream's own charter to close).
theActualDecision.compatibilityAdapters: None were needed or built. The task permits compatibility adapters where two pipelines produce genuinely overlapping facts that must converge on one source - investigation found the two pipelines' real, current outputs do NOT overlap in any of the six truth kinds examined (each row above resolves to exactly one owner, or to 'neither, disclosed'), so no adapter was required. This is the honest outcome of the investigation, not an assumption made in advance.

outOfScopeButWorthFlagging.finding: The actual, deployed covenant-capacity CALCULATION engine (lib/covenant-engine.ts, reading CovenantProvision rows) is powered TODAY by neither pipeline generation discussed in this map - grep-confirmed the only writers of CovenantProvision anywhere in this repository are prisma/seed.ts and lib/coherent.ts (both hand-authored, engineer-run population for the reference companies Coherent/Matthews, never a live application write path). Neither the legacy extraction+promotion pipeline nor this workstream's newly-live-wired contract-model pipeline feeds CovenantProvision at all.
outOfScopeButWorthFlagging.relevanceToBlocker10: This is a real, pre-existing, and larger gap than BLOCKER-10 itself (which is specifically about the safe-failure/review-event wiring, not about capacity-calculation data population) - it is disclosed here only because it is directly adjacent to, and easily confused with, this workstream's own scope. Closing BLOCKER-10 (proving a live analysis run reaches a real persisted review item) does NOT, and was never asked to, make a live-uploaded document's covenants computable by lib/covenant-engine.ts. That is a separate, substantially larger undertaking (a real CovenantProvision-population path from either pipeline generation) explicitly out of this bounded workstream's charter (no financial arithmetic, no simulation/dashboard, no Phase 4 work).

dispositionNote: The truth-ownership investigation is complete, evidence-based (real writer-tracing, not prose claims), and honestly discloses the one genuine remaining gap (durable semantic-claim/IR persistence) rather than glossing over it. The ownership decision itself (contract-model authoritative for structural/package-relationship/operative-state/review-state truth) is implemented and proven (14-18). Reserved CERTIFIED status for a future, independent recertification phase.
